title: Japan and South Korea Face Off Again in the US Navy’s Frigate Search
gist: The US Navy's search for a foreign frigate design — backed by $1.85 billion in the FY2027 budget proposal and shortlisted to Japan's upgraded Mogami, South Korea's Chungnam and Turkiye's Istanbul class — has opened a new front of Japan-South Korea defense-industrial competition, with up to two hulls potentially built overseas before production shifts to US yards.

insights.claim: USNI News reported on September 1 that the White House and US Navy are considering three allied frigate designs: Japan's upgraded Mogami class (the New FFM or 06FFM), South Korea's Chungnam class, and Turkiye's Istanbul class.
insights.speaker: Takahashi Kosuke
insights.so_what: A named three-way shortlist gives direct exposure candidates: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, HD Hyundai Heavy Industries and Turkish yards.

insights.claim: The Pentagon's fiscal year 2027 budget proposal included $1.85 billion for an effort involving foreign warship designs, with Japan and South Korea at the center of the discussion, per Naval News reporting in June.
insights.speaker: Takahashi Kosuke
insights.so_what: Budgeted money, not just interest — this raises the probability that a foreign-design frigate program actually proceeds and becomes a revenue event for the winner.
insights.quote: the Pentagon’s fiscal year 2027 budget proposal included $1.85 billion for an effort involving foreign warship designs
insights.locator: As Naval News reported in June

insights.claim: Up to two ships could be built overseas before production shifts to US yards, meaning the near-term export revenue to the winning foreign builder is capped while the long-term value lies in design licensing and technology transfer.
insights.speaker: Takahashi Kosuke
insights.so_what: Model the prize as IP and licensing plus prestige, not as a large multi-hull export order — relevant to sizing the earnings impact for the winner.
insights.locator: Up to two ships could be built overseas

insights.claim: The US Navy's interest in foreign frigate designs has opened a new front in Japan-South Korea defense industrial competition, pitting Mitsubishi Heavy Industries against HD Hyundai Heavy Industries.
insights.speaker: Takahashi Kosuke
insights.so_what: Tokyo-Seoul rivalry over US naval work is a recurring competitive dynamic with political spillover; watch it as a constraint on trilateral defense-industrial cooperation.
insights.quote: The U.S. Navy’s reported interest in foreign frigate designs has opened a new front in Japan-South Korea defense industrial competition.
insights.locator: The U.S. Navy’s reported interest in foreign frigate designs
